reason: Sliding the constant shows that integrating gives a family of curves, and that the point (4, 10) picks out the single curve with c = 3.

scenes.title: One gradient, many curves: the point fixes c
scenes.purpose: See that integrating gives a family of curves that differ only by the constant c, and that the point (4, 10) selects the one with c = 3.

elements.value: At $x=4$ the curve has $y = {2*4^(3/2) - 16/4^2 - 2*4 + c}$; it needs to be $10$.

steps.text: After rewriting as $3x^{\frac{1}{2}} + 32x^{-3} - 2$ and integrating term by term, you get $y = 2x^{\frac{3}{2}} - 16x^{-2} - 2x + c$. This is the M1 and the two A1 marks for the integration. Changing $c$ slides the whole curve up or down.

Drag the point $G$ along the curve and then change $c$. The tangent at a given $x$ stays parallel, because the gradient $3\sqrt{x} + \frac{32}{x^3} - 2$ does not contain $c$. That is why the gradient alone cannot fix $c$.
With $c=0$ the curve gives $y=7$ at $x=4$, which misses $(4,10)$. Substituting $x=4$, $y=10$ gives $10 = 16 - 1 - 8 + c$, so $c=3$. This is the A1 for finding $c$.
Set $c=3$: the curve passes through $(4, 10)$. So $y = 2x^{\frac{3}{2}} - \frac{16}{x^2} - 2x + 3$, the final A1. Leaving out $+c$ would force the curve through $y=7$ instead.

guide.what_you_see: A curve $C$ whose equation comes from integrating the given gradient, drawn with a constant $c$ you can change, together with the marked point $(4, 10)$ that the question says lies on the curve. A movable point and its tangent show the slope of the curve at any chosen $x$.

legend.meaning: The integrated curve $y=2x^{\frac{3}{2}}-16x^{-2}-2x+c$, drawn for $0.6\leqslant x\leqslant 8$; its shape depends on the slider value of $c$.
The given point $(4, 10)$, which the required curve must pass through.
A point you can drag along $C$ to pick the $x$-value at which the slope is shown.
The tangent to $C$ at $G$; its slope equals $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=3\sqrt{x}+\frac{32}{x^3}-2$ at that $x$.
A vertical guide line at $x=4$, the $x$-value of the given point.
A text note giving the height of the curve at $x=4$ for the current $c$, to compare with the required $10$.

interact.do: Move the slider between $-5$ and $8$, then set it to $0$ and finally to $3$.
interact.watch: The whole curve shifts vertically without changing shape. At $c=0$ it crosses $x=4$ at $y=7$, below $(4, 10)$; at $c=3$ it passes exactly through $(4, 10)$.

interact.do: Drag $G$ left and right along the curve, for example to $x=2$, then change $c$ while $G$ stays put.
interact.watch: At $x=2$ the tangent slope is $3\sqrt{2}+4-2\approx 6.24$. Changing $c$ moves the curve but the tangent stays parallel to its earlier direction, because $c$ does not appear in the gradient.

question_link.text: The curve $C$ is the family of solutions you get after rewriting and integrating, which earns the M1 and the integration A1 marks, and the tangent shows why the gradient cannot fix $c$. Substituting $x=4$, $y=10$ gives $10=16-1-8+c$, so $c=3$ (the A1 for $c$), and the curve through $P$ is the final equation $y=2x^{\frac{3}{2}}-\frac{16}{x^2}-2x+3$.

read_off: The note $val$ gives $2\times4^{\frac{3}{2}}-\frac{16}{4^2}-8+c=7+c$, the height of the curve at $x=4$; it must equal $10$, which happens when $c=3$.
